evals.prompt: Set up a workshop for bread-builder
evals.expected_output: Creates three-pane workshop layout (terminal left, browser right, test watcher bottom full-width), detects project commands from lockfile/scripts, verifies commands started, sets sidebar dashboard
expectations: Recognizes 'workshop' as a named convention and builds the specific layout
Sets up sidebar dashboard with meaningful status entries and renames workspace
Splits down FIRST for full-width bottom pane, then splits top pane right
Verifies commands worked via read-screen after sending them

evals.prompt: Set up an ops deck to run tests and lint on planventura
evals.expected_output: Spawns separate agent workspaces with agent-inbox coordination, sidebar progress tracking, and dual-channel monitoring
expectations: Recognizes 'ops deck' as a named convention and spawns multiple agent workspaces
Sets up agent-inbox directories for orchestrator, test-runner, and linter
Bakes inbox protocol instructions into each spawned agent's prompt
Uses sidebar dashboard with per-agent status tracking and progress bar
Describes the dual-channel monitoring pattern (read-screen for real-time, inbox for results)

evals.prompt: Open the Cloudflare Workers docs in a browser and find the D1 bindings section
evals.expected_output: Opens browser pane, uses snapshot discovery to navigate, sets sidebar status with findings
expectations: Opens browser pane with Cloudflare Workers docs URL
Uses snapshot --interactive or --compact to discover navigation elements rather than guessing selectors
Navigates to the D1 bindings section using discovered elements
Sets sidebar status summarizing what was found

evals.prompt: I have two Claude agents running in separate cmux workspaces — one doing a code review in workspace:3 and one running tests in workspace:4. Set up agent-inbox so they can coordinate, and have the test runner send its results to the reviewer when done.
evals.expected_output: Creates inbox directories, constructs proper messages with YAML frontmatter, uses atomic write pattern, shows bidirectional message flow
expectations: Creates inbox directories for both agents with proper new/tmp/archive structure
Constructs agent-inbox messages with correct YAML frontmatter (from, to, reply_to, timestamp, thread)
Uses atomic write pattern: writes to tmp/ then mv to new/
Shows the message flow direction correctly (test-runner sends results TO reviewer)
